title: Regional KV staleness during inter-region peering — emergency traffic orchestration hotpatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a partial inter-region network flapping event we observed progressive request latency increases for a subset of tenants due to asymmetric KV cache invalidation and stale routing metadata. This ticket tracks the emergency traffic orchestration hotpatch, customer communications, and follow-up permanent fixes.
steps_taken: 2026-03-01 04:12 UTC: Pager alert from latency-monitoring for us-east1-eu-west1 path — initial spike to p95 token latency +480ms for 12 tenants (alert group: infra-latency-p95)

2026-03-01 04:20 UTC: Triage call (pagerduty channel #inc-114512). Determined symptoms: long tail latency correlated with KV cache miss rate and increased 502s from model-proxy in eu-west1 when routed from us-east1
2026-03-01 04:35 UTC: Scoped blast radius — used tenant-routing-dashboard to identify affected tenant tags and prioritized high-ARPU customers for mitigation
2026-03-01 05:00 UTC: Deployed traffic-orchestration hotpatch: prefix-based sticky routing for affected tenant prefixes to keep traffic local while KV reconciliation completed (PR #4231).
2026-03-01 05:12 UTC: Applied temporary throttle and shed low-priority background batching to relieve proxy CPU pressure in eu-west1
2026-03-01 05:40 UTC: Opened support escalation thread with affected customer contacts and published interim status on trust portal
2026-03-02 08:00 UTC: Roll-forward hotfix 4231 validated in canary then rolled to 50% then 100% for affected prefixes; p95 returned to normal within 22 minutes of full rollforward
reproduction: Simulated cross-region peering instability in staging by injecting asymmetric packet loss between us-east1 and eu-west1 and replaying production request mix to observe KV cache invalidation race. Repro shows stale route table entries when invalidation acknowledgement lost. Steps saved in reproducer script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/ops/repro/kvcache-peering
root_cause_summary: KV cache invalidation relied on cross-region acknowledgement. When inter-region control-plane packets were dropped, one region did not receive a tombstone and continued to serve stale routing metadata. The serving runtime selects model variants based on that stale metadata causing mismatched model shard lookups and proxy timeouts.
mitigation_plan: Hotpatch (deployed): sticky prefix routing for affected tenant prefixes to avoid cross-region cache dependency during reconciliation (PR #4231)
Immediate follow-up: add per-tenant KV cache negative-ack timeout to force local tombstone after 10s of missing ack
Short-term (2 days): implement cross-region invalidation ack fallback over control-plane mesh and exponential backoff retries
Medium-term (2–4 weeks): redesign invalidation to use versioned, idempotent tombstones with vector-clock-like monotonic counters per-tenant
Customer communications: continue nightly updates until postmortem is published
rollback_plan: If hotpatch shows regressions, immediately revert PR #4231 and shift affected prefixes to pre-defined fallback region (eu-west1 -> eu-west1-standby) while we apply a safe cache flush. Rollback playbook documented in runbook link below.
postmortem_actions: Ensure control-plane telemetry for invalidation acks is retained for 90 days
Add synthetic chaos tests to CI that fuzzes control-plane packet loss and validates eventual cache convergence
Ship versioned tombstone implementation (owner: runtime/cache team)
Update Runbook: add a new 'KV invalidation asymmetric' section with checklist and customer messaging templates
Run a tabletop exercise with SRE, runtime, and support to rehearse the sticky-routing mitigation and rollback steps
